findings.title: TP is posted as a plain (non-reduce-only) GTX limit. After a stop-out it can open an opposite position, and the TIME exit then doubles that position
findings.file_line: core/intraday_lane.py:497-500 (TP via e.venue.limit_gtx); 515 (_venue_sync only tests amt==0); 564-572 (_exit_ioc sells abs(amt) on ps side)
findings.scenario: Long 1.5 SOL with a closePosition SELL stop at 99.75 and a 'TP' SELL limit_gtx 1.5 @100.4. That TP is an ordinary opening order (DemoVenue.limit_gtx has no reduceOnly; MockVenue files it as kind ENTRY, so it never expires with the position). Price drops to 99.70: the stop closes the position. Price then rallies to 100.45 before the lane's next _venue_sync (up to intraday_every_s; much longer if the lane is erroring, a TP cancel failed silently at 523/561, or the process restarted). The stale TP fills and opens a SHORT of -1.5. _venue_sync sees amt != 0 and keeps treating it as the long. At 45 min, _exit_ioc sends SELL abs(-1.5). Result: venue amt -3.0 with no stop, lane pos=None, e.busy=False, and the ledger books 'BUY TIME +36.0 bps (+0.540 U)'. Repro: scratchpad/rv_active/s2_tp_flip.py.
findings.fix: Place the TP with e.venue.take_profit(...) (reduce-only GTX through c.reduce_maker; returns False when price is already through the target). In _venue_sync and _exit_ioc, compare sign(amt) with ps['side']: a flat or opposite-sign position means the lane's position is gone, so settle it and do not trade abs(amt). Cap the IOC qty at min(abs(amt), ps['qty']) and, if possible, send it reduce-only.

findings.title: S2 active stop is trailed on the fill pass to the low of a 5m bar that closed BEFORE the fill. This bypasses the replay stop and the 5 bps minimum
findings.file_line: core/intraday_lane.py:402-406 (_trail called on every pass with a pos, including the fill pass); 535-550 (_trail uses f['b5'] last closed bar, no check that it closed after fill_t)
findings.scenario: S2_slope3_tp60 long is posted at EMA20 = 100.2222. The order_template/replay stop is s2_stop = 99.9346 (28.7 bps). The fill is detected on a non-5m-close pass: _active_bars -> _venue_sync -> _on_fill -> _trail. _trail moves the exchange stop to low[k] of the pre-fill bar: 100.2072, which is 1.5 bps, effectively inside the spread. s2_stop exists to forbid stops under 5 bps (sl_min_bps -> 1 ATR). The replay trails only at the next 5m close, using the bar that contains the fill. When low[k] is above the market instead, every pass does cancel stop -> -2021 reject -> re-place old stop, leaving a naked window each minute. Repro: scratchpad/rv_active/s9_trail_at_fill.py.
findings.fix: Trail only on 5m bars whose t_close > pos['fill_t'] (record the last trailed bar's t_close) and only when that bar is newly closed, matching on_bar line 310-312. Skip the trail when nb is on the wrong side of the current book.

findings.title: Stop rejected at fill plus an unfilled IOC leaves the position with no exchange stop until the 45 min TIME barrier ('retry next pass' never happens)
findings.file_line: core/intraday_lane.py:493-496 (STOP-REJECTED -> _exit_ioc then return); 573-576 (IOC miss only logs); 540 (_trail returns when sl_cid is None); 557-563 (TIME path cancels stops before the IOC)
findings.scenario: Entry fills. venue.stop raises (e.g. -2021 because price already traded through the stop, or a 5xx; DemoVenue.stop has no retry). _exit_ioc sends the IOC at ref*(1-15 bps), where ref is e.book() bid. The lane ignores book['stale'], and an empty vbook falls back to ps['entry']. The IOC returns (0,0). pos stays with sl_cid=None, tp_cid=None, busy=True. Later passes run only the TIME check and _trail, which returns because sl_cid is None. Repro (scratchpad/rv_active/s3_stop_rejected.py): ioc called at t=0 and next at t=2700 s, so the position was unprotected for 45 min while price fell to 99 and booked -109 bps. On the TIME path, the stops are already cancelled when the IOC misses, so each failed attempt leaves the position naked for at least one bar (about 60 s).
findings.fix: Keep a pending-exit flag that is retried on every pass, including the early _venue_sync branch of step(). Re-place the closePosition stop after a failed IOC, or fall back to a reduce-only market close (venue.close). Build the IOC reference price from a fresh venue book_ticker, not a stale or empty vbook.

findings.title: PARTIALLY_FILLED entry is ignored by _venue_sync, so the partial position has no exchange stop until expiry or the next 5m close
findings.scenario: S2 entry for 1.5 SOL rests at EMA20, and 0.75 trades on the demo book. BinanceVenue.order returns status 'PARTIALLY_FILLED', filled 0.75. _venue_sync acts only on status == 'FILLED', so no _on_fill runs and no stop is placed. busy=True also blocks MARIN adopt. The 0.75 position stays unprotected until the S2 cancel/re-anchor at the next 5m close (up to 5 min) or the S1 expiry. Repro (scratchpad/rv_active/s4_partial.py (a)): after 25 sync passes, venue amt 0.75, lane pos None, stops [].
findings.fix: On PARTIALLY_FILLED (filled > 0), place the closePosition stop immediately (it is qty-agnostic) and track the filled qty in pos while the remainder rests. Or cancel the remainder and call _on_fill with the filled qty.

findings.title: A partially filled IOC exit is booked as a full close: the residual has no stop and busy is released
findings.file_line: core/intraday_lane.py:571-574 (if got: self._close(...)); stops already cancelled at 557-563
findings.scenario: TIME exit on 1.5 SOL. TP and stop are cancelled, then the IOC SELL fills only 0.75 (thin demo book within the 15 bps cap). _close runs because got > 0: pos=None, e.busy=False, ledger row qty 1.5. The venue still holds 0.75 long with no stop and no TP. Engine.sync then ADOPTs it into MARIN with a different stop, or with adopt_external=False it stays naked and _free() (which ignores e.view amt) lets a new intraday entry net against it. Repro: scratchpad/rv_active/s4_partial.py (b), which shows venue amt 0.75, lane pos None, busy False, live {}.
findings.fix: Compare got with amt. If got < amt, reduce pos['qty'], keep pos and busy, re-place the closePosition stop, and retry the remainder (or close it reduce-only at market). Book only the qty actually filled.

findings.title: S2 re-anchor always raises TypeError: self.order['side'] is read after _cancel_entry has set self.order = None
findings.scenario: An S2 order is resting, and at the next 5m close s2_trend still equals the order side. _cancel_entry cancels the order, sets self.order=None and busy=False, then self.order['side'] raises TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable. step() aborts before line 388, so last_t is not advanced and 'INTRADAY error TypeError' is logged at every S2 re-anchor. The order is only re-posted on a later pass, as a fresh signal that must pass _free(); in the 4H quiet window or under the daily breaker the order is simply dropped, unlike the replay. Busy also drops to False between passes, so the trend lane can take the symbol. Repro: scratchpad/rv_active/s1_reanchor.py. Note: a naive fix that re-posts after a partial fill found by _cancel_entry would add a second entry on top of the new position.
findings.fix: Capture side = self.order['side'] before _cancel_entry. Re-post only when _cancel_entry returned 0 filled and self.pos is None.

findings.title: S1 one-minute expiry is checked only on passes that receive a new kline: orders live about 2 minutes, or indefinitely while mainnet klines come from cache
findings.file_line: core/intraday_lane.py:414 (expiry check inside _active_bars after the new-bar path); 368-371 (early branch only syncs); 402 (returns when new is empty); 427 (expire_t = clock()+60)
findings.scenario: (a) S1 order posted at C+11 s with expire_t = C+71. The next fetch pass at C+62.5 has clock < expire_t, so the order is kept, and the following fetch is at C+124. The order rests about 113 s and can fill in a minute the replay never trades (replay: only the bar after the 5m close). Repro: scratchpad/rv_active/s5_expiry_fetch.py (a). (b) fapi becomes unreachable: fetch_klines returns KLINE_CACHE (same rows), new is empty every pass, and _active_bars returns at 402. The S1 order rested for 30 min with busy=True, blocking the 4H trend lane for the whole outage. Repro: scratchpad/rv_active/s6_stale.py.
findings.fix: Evaluate order expiry (S1 by clock) in every pass, including step()'s early branch and when new is empty. Derive expire_t from the bar clock (end of the next 1m bar) rather than post time + 60.

findings.title: e.busy is set only after the awaited limit_gtx: another lane can start in that window, and its finally clears the intraday lane's busy flag
findings.scenario: While limit_gtx is in flight (one REST RTT), e.busy is still False. Engine._execute (engine.py:2055-2058) or TrendExecutor.step (trend_executor.py:341-347) sees busy False and starts, and its finally sets e.busy=False (engine.py:2385 / trend_executor.py:375) after the lane set it True. With the lane's order resting and busy False, Engine.sync ADOPTs the intraday fill as MARIN 'ADOPTED' and places a second closePosition SELL stop. Binance rejects a second stop per direction, so the lane gets STOP-REJECTED and IOC-closes MARIN's position. Repro: scratchpad/rv_active/s7_busy_race.py.
findings.fix: Set e.busy = True before awaiting limit_gtx and reset it in the except branch. Ideally use an owner token (e.g. e.busy_owner) so a lane only clears a flag it set.

findings.title: _cancel_entry swallows cancel errors, then drops tracking of an order that is still resting
findings.scenario: S1 expiry: venue.cancel raises (5xx retries exhausted or uncertain). The exception is swallowed. venue.order reports NEW with filled 0, so self.order=None and busy=False, but the GTX entry is still live. When it later fills, nobody owns it: Engine.sync adopts it into MARIN with MARIN's stop and hold rules. Repro: scratchpad/rv_active/s8_trail_cancel.py (b), which shows lane order None, busy False, live ENTRY, then MARIN pos ('ADOPTED', 1.5).
findings.fix: If the cancel failed and the status is still NEW or PARTIALLY_FILLED, keep self.order and busy and retry next pass, like Engine.orphans / retry_orphans.

findings.title: _trail cancels the stop first and has no close fallback when both re-placements fail
findings.scenario: S2 long, trail due. cancel_stop succeeds, then venue.stop(nb) raises (503 or -2021) and the fallback venue.stop(old sl) raises too. DemoVenue.stop has no retry, and both calls are back-to-back. The exception escapes, the position has no exchange stop, and ps['sl_cid'] still names the cancelled stop. Nothing closes the position: S1 never trails, and S2 retries only on the next bar. TrendExecutor.break_even closes ('STOP-LOST') in the same situation. Repro: scratchpad/rv_active/s8_trail_cancel.py (a), which shows live stops [] with amt 1.5.
findings.fix: Wrap the fallback. If it also fails, close the position at once (IOC or a reduce-only market close) and settle it, as TrendExecutor.break_even does.

findings.title: The stop cid is recorded only after a successful placement: an uncertain stop failure leaves an orphan closePosition stop
findings.scenario: venue.stop times out after Binance accepted the algo order. self.pos['sl_cid'] is never set, so _exit_ioc('STOP-REJECTED') cancels nothing and closes the position, leaving a live closePosition SELL stop. Binance allows one closePosition stop per direction, so the next intraday, trend or MARIN long gets its stop rejected, and the orphan can also close another lane's position when price reaches it.
findings.fix: Set pos['sl_cid'] = cid before the call, and on any exception call cancel_stop(cid) (or query by clientAlgoId) before falling back to the IOC exit.

findings.title: Active ledger and daily breaker use inferred exits, not venue fills
findings.scenario: (1) TP partially fills 50% at 100.4, then the closePosition stop closes the rest. The TP status is PARTIALLY_FILLED, so the whole qty is booked as 'SL' at ps['sl'] with taker fees. (2) The stop fires between _venue_sync and _exit_ioc's position_view: amt==0, so the trade is booked as 'TP' at ps['tp'] with maker fees, turning a loss into a win. (3) In the flip case above, a real loss was booked as +36 bps. day_pnl is fed from these rows, so intraday_daily_kill_usdt can fail to trip. CLAUDE.md requires unknown fields to stay UNKNOWN rather than be modeled.
findings.fix: Settle from venue data: the stop and TP order avg/executedQty, or venue.realized_parts(symbol, entry_ms). Mark how and exit as UNKNOWN when they cannot be confirmed.

findings.title: Active S2 re-anchor always crashes (TypeError): the order is cancelled and never re-posted
findings.scenario: Active mode with an S2 variant. A resting S2 entry reaches the next 5m close and s2_trend still equals the order side, so the elif branch runs. _cancel_entry() sets self.order = None (line 476), and the next line evaluates self.order['side'], which raises TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable. Reproduced with MockVenue and a real Engine (scratchpad rv_integ/s2_reanchor.py): EXC TypeError, then order None and busy False. Every S2 entry is cancelled at the first 5m close after posting and never re-anchored, so active S2 behaves differently from the replay. intraday_loop logs 'INTRADAY error TypeError' every 5 minutes. The partial-fill branch of _cancel_entry still runs _on_fill and then raises.
findings.fix: Capture side = self.order['side'] (and v) before await self._cancel_entry(), and re-post only if self.pos is None afterwards. Keep e.busy True across the cancel and re-post (do not clear it in _cancel_entry on this path). Otherwise the trend executor can claim the symbol during the limit_gtx await, and its finally block then clears the lane's busy flag.

findings.title: Burst lane and intraday lane both trade one SOL/DOGE net position in active mode; intraday's close logic acts on the whole net amount
findings.scenario: Both lanes active on SOLUSDT. Burst never sets e.busy or e.pos: its position is lane-local (burst_lane.py:248). Burst holds 0.6 SOL long, then at the next 5m close intraday _free() sees trend_owned False, e.pos None, e.busy False and posts BUY 1.5, which fills. The net position is 2.1 and the intraday closePosition SELL stop now covers all 2.1. (1) If burst exits first, intraday is unaffected. (2) If the intraday stop fires, it closes burst's 0.6 too. Burst still thinks it is long, so its non-reduce-only TP SELL can open a short. (3) _venue_sync only detects its own exit when the net amt == 0 (line 515), so while burst holds anything the stop exit is missed. The later TIME exit then IOC-sells abs(view.amt) (lines 564-572), which includes the other lane's quantity.
findings.fix: Make _free() also refuse when abs(e.view.get('amt') or 0) > 0 or when another lane has an order or position (e.g. a shared per-engine lane-owner token instead of the boolean e.busy). Have the burst lane claim it too. Size intraday exits by the lane's own qty, not the net amt, and use reduceOnly orders.

findings.title: Intraday TP is a plain GTX limit (not reduce-only): after the stop closes the position, the TP can open a new unprotected position
findings.scenario: Active long 1.5 SOL with a TP SELL 1.5 at 100.4 placed via venue.limit_gtx, which has no reduceOnly flag (DemoVenue.limit_gtx). The engine itself uses venue.take_profit -> reduce_maker. The closePosition stop fires at 99.75. The TP is cancelled only on the next _venue_sync, up to intraday_every_s = 10 s later. If price whipsaws back through 100.4 in that window, the TP fills and opens a SHORT 1.5 with no stop. _venue_sync then sees amt = -1.5 != 0 and still treats the long as open. At the TIME exit, _exit_ioc sends 'SELL' abs(amt) (ps side > 0), which doubles the short to 3 SOL.
findings.fix: Place the TP with e.venue.take_profit(...) (reduce-only GTX). Send the TIME-exit IOC as reduce-only. Compare the venue amt sign and size with the lane's own position instead of only checking amt == 0.

findings.title: Active lane state is memory-only: after a restart the micro engine adopts the intraday position and the lane's TP and stop are orphaned
findings.scenario: Active intraday holds a SOL long with its closePosition stop and GTX TP resting. The process restarts (run.bat demo relaunch, crash, or activate() re-run). The new IntradayLane starts with order = pos = None and e.busy False. Engine.sync then sees view.amt != 0, adopt_external = True (demo default, engine.py:221), not busy and not trend_owned, and MARIN adopts the position (reusing the found STOP). The non-reduce-only intraday TP is left on the book. Once the micro engine exits the adopted position, that TP can still fill and open a fresh unprotected position. TrendExecutor persists data/trend_active.json for exactly this case; the intraday lane does not.
findings.fix: Persist order/pos (cids, qty, sl/tp) atomically, as TrendExecutor does, and restore them in __init__ (setting e.busy / an owner flag before the first Engine.sync). Or, on start-up in active mode, cancel any gI-/gIS-/gIT- orders and refuse to run until reconciled.

findings.title: 4H trend lane blocked by intraday's e.busy for up to 45 min: the quiet window only covers the 10 min AFTER a 4H close
findings.scenario: Active mode. An S1 entry fills at 03:58 UTC: t % 14400 = 13080 >= 600, so _free allows it. _on_fill sets e.busy = True for up to intraday_hold_min = 45 min. At the 04:00 4H close, TrendExecutor.step hits `if e.busy or e.pos: continue` on every 60 s pass until about 04:43-04:45. The trend entry is delayed 45 min from the bar close that its replay prices, despite the docstring promising the 4H close window is reserved for the trend lane. Once the S2 re-anchor crash is fixed, an S2 entry can be re-anchored indefinitely while its trend condition holds (no expiry, and _free is not re-checked on re-anchor). The trend lane would then be blocked for hours in exactly the trending regimes it trades.
findings.fix: Block new intraday entries from (4H close - intraday_hold_min - entry window) through the close, not only after it. Or force-exit or cancel intraday orders/positions before each 4H close. Also cap S2 resting time and re-check _free() on every re-anchor.

findings.title: Trailing-stop replacement can leave the active position with no exchange stop
findings.scenario: Active S2 long. _trail cancels the current closePosition stop (543-546), then places a new one at the last 5m low, which is rejected: e.g. -2021 'would immediately trigger' after a drop in the current minute, or a transient 5xx. The fallback re-place at the old level (line 552) also fails with a transient error. The exception propagates to intraday_loop and is only logged. ps['sl_cid'] still names the cancelled stop, so the position is unprotected until a later pass happens to re-place it. If the 5m low no longer improves, `better` is False and nothing re-places it until the 45-min TIME exit. TrendExecutor.break_even handles the same double failure by closing the position ('STOP-LOST').
findings.fix: Wrap the fallback stop in try/except. On failure, call _exit_ioc('STOP-LOST') (or retry and then close), mirroring trend_executor.break_even. Set ps['sl_cid'] = None when the old stop has been cancelled.

findings.title: Shadow lane is not the replay under the production profile (shared slot across variants plus extra gates); the equality test only covers one variant with the gates off
findings.scenario: Demo runs intraday_variants = ('S1_SESSION', 'S2_slope3_tp60') in one lane with one position slot. The replay runs each variant independently, and the verdict is per (symbol, strategy). The lane also applies the 4H quiet window, the daily kill, and the real engine's trend_owned/e.pos/e.busy to virtual trades; the replay has none of these. fake_engine sets quiet_s = 0 and kill = 1e9, and the equality test runs a single variant. On a 12 000-bar synthetic walk (scratchpad rv_integ/cmp.py) with the production profile: S1_SESSION had 15 shadow trades vs 20 in the replay (14 in common), and S2 had 37 vs 38. While the active 4H trend lane holds a symbol (trend_owned, often for days), the shadow lane records nothing on that symbol. The shadow ledger cannot be compared to the replay verdicts it is meant to check.
findings.fix: In shadow mode, run one independent virtual book per variant and skip the real-occupancy, quiet-window and kill gates (or log them as would_block fields). Alternatively, add the same gates to tools/intraday_replay.py. Add a test that uses the production defaults.

findings.title: Lane test fails at HEAD: default variant changed to S1_SESSION but the active-gate test still expects S1_ROLL100
findings.scenario: Commit 0fd4a27 changed Profile.intraday_variants from ('S1_ROLL100', ...) to ('S1_SESSION', ...). test_active_refused_without_verdict_and_on_live builds the lane from the demo profile with a verdict marking S1_ROLL100 eligible, so _mode finds no match and returns 'shadow'. The assert lane2.mode == 'active' fails. `python -m pytest -q` reports 3 failed: this one, plus two unrelated environment failures (missing data/ and tools/check_models_live.py). The repo's mandatory zero-regression gate is red, and the active-gate positive path is no longer tested.
findings.fix: Pass intraday_variants=('S1_ROLL100',) in that test's fake_engine call, or write the verdict for S1_SESSION.

findings.title: Active ledger books planned prices as realized: stop exits at the stop level, and an unknown flat position at the TP price
findings.scenario: When _venue_sync finds amt == 0 with the TP not FILLED, it writes exit = ps['sl'] with a taker fee, but the STOP_MARKET actually filled with slippage or a gap. In _exit_ioc, if the position is already flat (e.g. the exchange stop fired between _venue_sync and the TIME exit, or a lagging position_view right after STOP-REJECTED), it books exit_how 'TP' at ps['tp'] with a maker fee: a stop-out recorded as a win. data/intraday_trades.jsonl net_bps and net_usd are then fabricated rather than UNKNOWN. TrendExecutor uses venue.realized_parts for its ledger.
findings.fix: Query the stop/TP fills or venue.realized_parts(symbol, fill_ms) for the exit price and fees. When the exit cannot be attributed, write exit_how 'UNKNOWN' and leave the price/PnL fields null.

findings.title: With a local clock ahead of Binance, the lane fetches 2 s after the close and treats the still-open 1m bar as closed
findings.scenario: step() fetches as soon as local now >= last_t + 122 s, and fetch_klines keeps rows with close_time < local now_ms. With the PC clock 3 s fast, a pass at local 10:02:02.5 (server 10:01:59.5) receives the in-progress 10:01 candle (close_time 10:01:59.999). It passes both filters and goes through on_bar with partial h/l/c and partial taker-buy volume. At a 5m close, that partial bar's CVD drives s1_signal. It is never re-processed, because only t > last_t is new. Shadow then diverges from the replay on those bars.
findings.fix: Fetch only after a larger margin (e.g. 5-10 s), or use the server time offset from the venue client. Alternatively, drop the last row unless the next candle exists (Binance returns the open candle as the last row).

verify:active-venue:0.evidence:
Code trace: core/intraday_lane.py:499 posts the TP with e.venue.limit_gtx. In the demo venue that resolves to BinanceVenue.limit_gtx (core/engine.py:807), which calls DemoVenue.limit_gtx (live/radar_auto_trader.py:293). That sends a plain LIMIT GTX with positionSide BOTH and no reduceOnly, so once the position is gone it is an ordinary opening order. The venue already has a reduce-only TP primitive, take_profit (radar_auto_trader.py:311, through c.reduce_maker), and the engine's own bracket uses it, but the lane does not. MockVenue/ShadowVenue (radar_auto_trader.py:420) files this TP as kind 'ENTRY', so it does not expire with the position the way 'TP'/'SL' do (line 476).

_venue_sync (intraday_lane.py:515) only checks `not amt`. _exit_ioc (intraday_lane.py:565-571) sends abs(amt) on ps['side']'s close side and never checks sign(amt).

Ran scratchpad/rv_active/s2_tp_flip.py:
- Long 1.5 @100, stop 99.75, TP SELL 1.5 @100.4.
- Quote drops to 99.70: the stop closes the position (amt 0) and the TP is still live as ENTRY.
- Quote rallies to 100.45: amt is -1.5.
- lane._venue_sync: pos side stays +1 and busy stays True.
- After 46 min, _active_bars runs the TIME exit: venue amt -3.0, lane pos None, busy False, no live orders. The event logged is 'INTRADAY BUY SOLUSDT S1_ROLL100 TIME +36.0 bps (+0.540 U)'.

Control (scratchpad/rv_verify_tp/v.py) on the same path, with only the TP routed through venue.take_profit: amt is 0.0 after the rally and the lane books SL -33.0 bps with busy False.

Other failures from the same root cause:
- If the TP cancel at 520-523 fails, the error is swallowed and the orphan opening order outlives the lane's position.
- If the TP fills between the position_view and the order query at 518, it is booked as 'TP' while the venue holds a new naked position.

Limits:
- The stop-then-rally window is normally at most about intraday_every_s (10 s) plus REST latency. It is longer when step raises (intraday_loop swallows the error and sleeps).
- Active mode is demo-only and is currently blocked because every verdict in config/intraday_verdict.json is SHADOW.
- Engine sync may later ADOPT the doubled position and put a stop on it, but the size is still doubled and the ledger row is still false.
verify:active-venue:0.fix:
1. In _on_fill (intraday_lane.py:497-500), place the TP with `ok = await e.venue.take_profit(sym, close_side, qty, tp, cid)`. take_profit is reduce-only GTX. If it returns False, the price is already through the target: take the exit right away, or leave tp_cid None.
2. In _venue_sync (515) and _exit_ioc (565), read the signed amt. If amt is 0 or sign(amt) != ps['side'], treat the lane's position as closed: settle it, cancel the TP and stop, and never trade abs(amt).
3. In _exit_ioc, use qty = min(abs(amt), ps['qty']). Send it reduce-only, for example with a reduce-only IOC variant or venue.close/reduce_position.

findings.title: BTC shadow book silently records nothing between $75k and $100k: _qty returns 0 under BTCUSDT's $100 min notional and the signal is dropped
findings.file_line: core/intraday_lane.py:259-265 (_qty) and :330-332 (drop); enabled for BTC by core/engine.py:494 intraday_symbols
findings.scenario: Demo profile, BTCUSDT, wallet $5,000. notional = min(150, 0.04*5000) = 150. At px = 80,000: q = floor(150/80000/0.001)*0.001 = 0.001, so q*px = $80, which is below spec['min_notional'] = 100 (FALLBACK_SPECS and the Binance BTCUSDT filter), and _qty returns 0.0.
